newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank sells $250 mln to support lev H1.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank sells $250 mln to support lev H1.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said it has spent some $250 million net of its foreign exchange reserves for interventions on the local interbank market in the first half of this year.
"Net (foreign currency) sales of $249.7 million to local banks contributed for some 38 percent of the fall of central bank reserves from January through June," the BNB said in its semi-annual report.
The lev fell from 70 per dollar on the interbank market in January to 155 at the end of June. It has persistently declined since then to 240 per dollar today.

Reserves fell by a total of $663 million to $573.4 million in the first half due to interest and principal payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt and net foreign currency sales to local banks, BNB figures showed.
The central bank also sold $231.7 million to the Finance Ministry in the first half to support foreign debt payments, which contributed for some 37 percent of the total fall in reserves.
Direct BNB payments to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) totalled $178 million in the first half.

Under Bulgaria's budget regulations, payments to the IMF are serviced through central bank reserves while debt payments to the London Club of commercial creditors and to the Paris Club of government lenders are part of the state budget expenditure.
Uncertainty over delayed IMF funding has restricted BNB's ability to sustain a long term support for the lev through interventions on the local interbank forex market, forex dealers said.
The BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said last week that the central bank planned to support a gradual lev depreciation against the dollar as much as it could.
"However, this policy is largely conditional on proceeds from privatisation and IMF funding," Filipov said.

The IMF has twice postponed a second $115 million tranche of funding under a standby agreement until the Socialist government meets funding requirements to close down loss makers and speed up privatisation.
An IMF mission is expected in Sofia this week to review the government's reform performance. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
